title: Notification Preferences — Backend Schema & API
description: Extend the user settings API to store and return per-type notification preferences. Add the notifications object to the user settings schema and validate incoming values.

unknowns.description: Will adding a 'notifications' column to user_settings require a migration on the existing table or a new table?
unknowns.resolution: New JSONB column on user_settings. Migration is non-destructive — existing rows default to null and the API returns sensible defaults.

tasks.description: Write migration: add notifications JSONB column to user_settings
Update PATCH /api/user/settings to accept and validate notifications object
Return notifications in GET /api/user/settings with defaults when null
Write integration tests for the updated endpoint

architecture_decisions.decision: Store preferences as JSONB on user_settings rather than a separate notifications_preferences table
options_considered: Separate table with one row per preference type
architecture_decisions.rationale: The preference set is small and read as a unit. JSONB is simpler and avoids a join on every settings fetch. If preferences grow complex, a separate table is easy to migrate to.

test_scenarios.description: GET /api/user/settings returns notifications object with all three defaults for a user with no saved preferences
PATCH with valid notifications object saves correctly and is returned on next GET
PATCH with unknown notification type returns 422

no_gos: Email sending logic — this scope is persistence only
